zones.bz-belize-blue-hole: Belize and the Great Blue Hole
zones.gp-basseterre-cousteau: Cousteau Reserve and the leeward coast
zones.hr-dalmatie-brac: Bol and the island of Brač
zones.br-santacatarina-floripa: Joaquina, Praia Mole and Santa Catarina island

fr-landes-hossegor--le-pastis-landais.title: Pastis landais
fr-landes-hossegor--le-pastis-landais.text: A brioche flavored with orange blossom, rum or vanilla, long reserved for weddings and village festivals.

fr-landes-hossegor--la-course-landaise.title: Course landaise
fr-landes-hossegor--la-course-landaise.text: Écarteurs dodge the cow at the last moment, with no killing. It brightens local festivals from March to October.

fr-landes-hossegor--baine.title: Baïne
fr-landes-hossegor--baine.text: Gascon word for the pool of water running parallel to the beach, where the current can turn dangerous depending on the tide.

fr-paysbasque-guethary--l-axoa.title: Axoa
fr-paysbasque-guethary--l-axoa.text: Diced veal simmered with pepper, onion and Espelette chili: a dish of fairs and festivals in the Basque Country.

fr-paysbasque-guethary--kaixo.title: Kaixo
fr-paysbasque-guethary--kaixo.text: “Hello” or “hi” in Basque, to be said with a smile.

fr-paysbasque-guethary--les-fetes-de-la-.title: Saint-Nicolas festivals
fr-paysbasque-guethary--les-fetes-de-la-.text: Guéthary’s patron saint festivals take place every year in December, around Saint Nicholas.

fr-paysbasque-guethary--la-pelote-au-gra.title: Grand chistera pelota
fr-paysbasque-guethary--la-pelote-au-gra.text: The L’Olharroa club, founded in 1922, is nicknamed the Mecca of the grand chistera: games are played on the village wall.

fr-finistere-penhors--le-pardon-de-penho.title: Pardon de Penhors
fr-finistere-penhors--le-pardon-de-penho.text: The Penhors pardon, in Pouldreuzic, takes place on the first Sunday of September: procession, mass and blessing, like any Breton pardon.

fr-finistere-penhors--le-fest-noz.title: Fest-noz
fr-finistere-penhors--le-fest-noz.text: A Breton dance night open to all: you join the gavotte or the an dro after watching the steps.

fr-finistere-penhors--le-far-breton.title: Far breton
fr-finistere-penhors--le-far-breton.text: A cake of eggs, milk and salted butter, often with the prunes that Breton sailors brought back from Bordeaux.

fr-finistere-penhors--la-coiffe-bigouden.title: The Bigouden headdress
fr-finistere-penhors--la-coiffe-bigouden.text: About thirty centimeters tall, it is now worn only at pardons, celebrations and festivals.

fr-var-portcros--l-aioli.title: Aïoli
fr-var-portcros--l-aioli.text: Cod and vegetables served with a sauce of crushed garlic and olive oil: an emblematic dish of Provence.

fr-var-portcros--une-peche-encadree.title: Regulated fishing
fr-var-portcros--une-peche-encadree.text: On the island, fishing remains traditional but regulated: a charter since 1999 for 24 professionals, an annual permit for amateurs.

fr-var-portcros--la-vigie.title: La Vigie
fr-var-portcros--la-vigie.text: A former semaphore station reached by the old strategic road, with a panorama of the archipelago and the Maures massif.

fr-corse-rondinara--le-fiadone.title: Fiadone
fr-corse-rondinara--le-fiadone.text: A fresh cake made with brocciu, sugar, eggs and lemon, an emblematic dessert of Corsica.

fr-corse-rondinara--les-polyphonies-cors.title: Corsican polyphony
fr-corse-rondinara--les-polyphonies-cors.text: Three-voice a cappella singing, born of village and shepherd life: vigils, pilgrimages and festivals keep it alive.

fr-corse-rondinara--la-semaine-sainte-a-.title: Holy Week in Bonifacio
fr-corse-rondinara--la-semaine-sainte-a-.text: Brotherhoods hold well-attended processions during Holy Week, along with the Tenebrae services.

pt-ericeira--l-oursin-d-ericeira.title: Ericeira sea urchin
pt-ericeira--l-oursin-d-ericeira.text: A specialty of the town: village restaurants cook sea urchin in several ways during the festival dedicated to it.

pt-ericeira--le-festival-international-d.title: International Sea Urchin Festival
pt-ericeira--le-festival-international-d.text: Tastings, cooking shows and workshops at Ericeira’s municipal market: the 2026 edition ran from April 24 to May 3.

pt-ericeira--reserve-mondiale-de-surf.title: World Surfing Reserve
pt-ericeira--reserve-mondiale-de-surf.text: Since October 2011, the Ericeira coast has held the title of World Surfing Reserve, awarded by Save the Waves.

es-minorque-macarella--sant-joan-a-ciuta.title: Sant Joan in Ciutadella
es-minorque-macarella--sant-joan-a-ciuta.text: On June 23 and 24, riders and Menorcan horses parade through Ciutadella, with “bots” where the horse rears up.

es-minorque-macarella--le-fromage-de-mao.title: Maó cheese
es-minorque-macarella--le-fromage-de-mao.text: A cow’s milk cheese with an orange rind rubbed with olive oil and paprika, protected by a PDO since 1985.

es-minorque-macarella--la-caldereta-de-l.title: Caldereta de langosta
es-minorque-macarella--la-caldereta-de-l.text: A simmered spiny lobster stew, a typical dish of Menorca.

es-minorque-macarella--pomada.title: Pomada
es-minorque-macarella--pomada.text: Menorcan gin mixed with lemonade, drunk during the patron saint festivals.

es-minorque-macarella--le-cami-de-cavall.title: Camí de Cavalls
es-minorque-macarella--le-cami-de-cavall.text: A trail around the island on foot (GR 223), an old path that once linked the defense towers.

gr-zakynthos-navagio--la-fete-de-saint-d.title: Feast of Saint Dionysios
gr-zakynthos-navagio--la-fete-de-saint-d.text: On August 24, the relics of Saint Dionysios, patron of the island, are carried in procession in the evening through Zakynthos town.

gr-zakynthos-navagio--le-raisin-de-corin.title: Zante currant
gr-zakynthos-navagio--le-raisin-de-corin.text: A small, sweet, seedless grape born on the island: along with olive oil, it is one of the island’s major products.

gr-zakynthos-navagio--les-produits-du-te.title: Local products
gr-zakynthos-navagio--les-produits-du-te.text: Olive oil, thyme honey, currants and wine are sold at roadside stalls and in the villages.

gr-zakynthos-navagio--le-poete-solomos.title: The poet Solomos
gr-zakynthos-navagio--le-poete-solomos.text: A statue of the poet Dionýsios Solomós adorns Zakynthos town’s main square, and a museum bears his name on Saint Mark’s Square.

gb-gower-rhossili--le-laverbread.title: Laverbread
gb-gower-rhossili--le-laverbread.text: A thick purée of porphyra seaweed boiled for hours, called “bara lawr” in Welsh.

gb-gower-rhossili--les-coques-de-penclaw.title: Penclawdd cockles
gb-gower-rhossili--les-coques-de-penclaw.text: Penclawdd families have gathered cockles from the Burry Inlet for generations; they are sold at Swansea market.

gb-gower-rhossili--l-agneau-de-pre-sale-.title: Gower salt marsh lamb
gb-gower-rhossili--l-agneau-de-pre-sale-.text: It grazes on samphire and sea lavender; PDO in the United Kingdom in 2021, then in the European Union in 2023.

gb-gower-rhossili--worm-s-head.title: Worm’s Head
gb-gower-rhossili--worm-s-head.text: Two islets, Inner Head and Outer Head, that can only be reached at low tide.

gb-gower-rhossili--gallois-au-nord-angla.title: Welsh in the north, English in the south
gb-gower-rhossili--gallois-au-nord-angla.text: Northern Gower has many Welsh speakers, while the south is traditionally English-speaking.

pf-societe-tahiti--le-heiva-i-tahiti.title: Heiva i Tahiti
pf-societe-tahiti--le-heiva-i-tahiti.text: Each July, about two weeks of song and dance contests and ancestral sports like va’a, at Place To’atā.

pf-societe-tahiti--le-poisson-cru.title: Poisson cru
pf-societe-tahiti--le-poisson-cru.text: Fish marinated in lime juice and coconut milk: the island dish to try first.

pf-societe-tahiti--le-tamaaraa.title: Tamaaraa
pf-societe-tahiti--le-tamaaraa.text: A feast of pork, fish and breadfruit steamed in an earth oven, for big family occasions.

pf-societe-tahiti--la-fleur-de-tiare.title: The tiaré flower
pf-societe-tahiti--la-fleur-de-tiare.text: A flower behind the left ear says you are not looking for company; behind the right, that you are available.

cl-pichilemu--la-fete-du-cochayuyo.title: Cochayuyo festival
cl-pichilemu--la-fete-du-cochayuyo.text: Five days of dishes made with cochayuyo, a sea algae; the last day fell on Sunday, July 26 in 2026.

cl-pichilemu--les-fiestas-patrias.title: Fiestas Patrias
cl-pichilemu--les-fiestas-patrias.text: Around September 18, Pichilemu celebrates the national holiday: traditional games, food, music and dance, day and night.

cl-pichilemu--empanadas-et-completos.title: Empanadas and completos
cl-pichilemu--empanadas-et-completos.text: Empanadas and “completos” are the two great takeaway classics in Pichilemu.

cl-pichilemu--le-parc-agustin-ross.title: Agustín Ross Park
cl-pichilemu--le-parc-agustin-ross.text: The Agustín Ross park and cultural center is one of Pichilemu’s five national monuments.

br-noronha--le-centre-historique.title: The historic center
br-noronha--le-centre-historique.text: Vila dos Remédios and the São Pedro dos Pescadores chapel are Brazilian cultural heritage, listed by Iphan in 2017.

br-noronha--l-acai.title: Açaí
br-noronha--l-acai.text: After a dive, nothing beats a bowl of açaí served at the port, with granola and bananas.

mx-islamujeres--le-tik-n-chik.title: Tik-n-chik
mx-islamujeres--le-tik-n-chik.text: A whole fish marinated in achiote, then grilled: the island’s signature dish.

mx-islamujeres--punta-sur.title: Punta Sur
mx-islamujeres--punta-sur.text: At the southern tip, the ruins of an old lighthouse and of a temple to Ixchel, goddess of fertility.

mx-islamujeres--isla-mujeres.title: Isla Mujeres
mx-islamujeres--isla-mujeres.text: The island’s name means “Island of Women” in Spanish.

sn-dakar-ouakam--le-ceebu-jen.title: Ceebu jën
sn-dakar-ouakam--le-ceebu-jen.text: Rice with fish and seasonal vegetables, born among Saint-Louis fishermen, UNESCO-listed in 2021; often eaten by hand.

sn-dakar-ouakam--teranga.title: Teranga
sn-dakar-ouakam--teranga.text: A Wolof word often translated as “hospitality”: sharing your meal and welcoming strangers into your home.

sn-dakar-ouakam--un-village-lebou.title: A Lebou village
sn-dakar-ouakam--un-village-lebou.text: Ouakam is one of the four original Lebou villages of the Cap-Vert peninsula, with Yoff, Ngor and Hann.

sn-dakar-ouakam--la-mosquee-de-la-divini.title: Mosque of the Divinity
sn-dakar-ouakam--la-mosquee-de-la-divini.text: A holy man said he received an order in a dream, on June 28, 1973, to build this mosque by the ocean.

au-whitsundays-whitehaven--le-great-barr.title: Great Barrier Reef Festival
au-whitsundays-whitehaven--le-great-barr.text: Four days in Airlie Beach with fireworks, a regatta of recycled boats and a street parade: July 31 to August 2 in 2026.

au-whitsundays-whitehaven--la-hamilton-i.title: Hamilton Island Race Week
au-whitsundays-whitehaven--la-hamilton-i.text: A major offshore regatta, described as Australia’s biggest: August 15 to 22 in 2026, with entertainment at the marina.

au-whitsundays-whitehaven--le-marche-d-a.title: Airlie Beach market
au-whitsundays-whitehaven--le-marche-d-a.text: Every Saturday from 7 a.m. to 1 p.m., on the waterfront: souvenirs, coffee, fresh fruit and local art.

au-whitsundays-whitehaven--le-ngaro-trac.title: Ngaro Track
au-whitsundays-whitehaven--le-ngaro-trac.text: Opened in 2026, this 32 km trail runs from Whitehaven to Hill Inlet; the traditional owners ask you to walk it with respect.

au-whitsundays-whitehaven--whitsunday.title: Whitsunday
au-whitsundays-whitehaven--whitsunday.text: James Cook passed the islands on Sunday, June 3, 1770, the day of Pentecost (Whitsun), hence their name.

us-hawaii-kona--le-cafe-de-kona.title: Kona coffee
us-hawaii-kona--le-cafe-de-kona.text: Only coffee from the slopes of Hualālai and Mauna Loa can be called Kona; a “Kona blend” requires just 10%.

us-hawaii-kona--le-kona-coffee-cultural-.title: Kona Coffee Cultural Festival
us-hawaii-kona--le-kona-coffee-cultural-.text: Since 1970, a ten-day coffee festival in November; the next edition is announced for November 5 to 14, 2027.

us-hawaii-kona--aloha.title: Aloha
us-hawaii-kona--aloha.text: A Hawaiian word for love, peace and compassion; it is also used to say hello and goodbye.

us-hawaii-kona--mahalo.title: Mahalo
us-hawaii-kona--mahalo.text: A Hawaiian word meaning thanks, gratitude and esteem.

us-hawaii-kona--pu-uhonua-o-honaunau.title: Puʻuhonua o Hōnaunau
us-hawaii-kona--pu-uhonua-o-honaunau.text: Near Kealakekua, this place of refuge saved anyone who had broken a kapu: a priest pardoned them, and they left free.

mu-lemorne--le-dholl-puri.title: Dholl puri
mu-lemorne--le-dholl-puri.text: A flatbread of Indian origin that has become the Mauritian “fish and chips.”

mu-lemorne--les-gateaux-piments.title: Gâteaux piments
mu-lemorne--les-gateaux-piments.text: Savory fritters, a variant of Indian vadai: literally chili cakes.

mu-lemorne--maha-shivaratri-a-ganga-tala.title: Maha Shivaratri at Ganga Talao
mu-lemorne--maha-shivaratri-a-ganga-tala.text: In February or March, for Maha Shivaratri, Mauritian Hindus make a pilgrimage to the crater lake of Ganga Talao.

mu-lemorne--le-sega.title: Séga
mu-lemorne--le-sega.text: Born among the enslaved of Mauritius and Réunion, it is played with ravanne, maravanne and triangle; UNESCO-listed in 2014.

mu-lemorne--le-morne-brabant.title: Le Morne Brabant
mu-lemorne--le-morne-brabant.text: UNESCO-listed in 2008, the mountain carries the legend of fleeing slaves who supposedly jumped from the rock in 1835 rather than be recaptured.

gp-desirade-petiteterre--la-fet-a-kabrit.title: Fèt a kabrit
gp-desirade-petiteterre--la-fet-a-kabrit.text: At Easter weekend, La Désirade celebrates the goat: it is the island’s big event, along with the Gwadarun.

gp-desirade-petiteterre--les-fetes-d-aou.title: August festivals
gp-desirade-petiteterre--les-fetes-d-aou.text: August 13 to 17: patron saint festival on the 15th, traditional sailors’ festival on the 16th, then the festival of lost sailors on the 17th.

gp-desirade-petiteterre--les-chantes-noe.title: Chantés Noël
gp-desirade-petiteterre--les-chantes-noe.text: Every December, Christmas carols are sung all over the island, sometimes in private homes.

gp-desirade-petiteterre--le-colombo.title: Colombo
gp-desirade-petiteterre--le-colombo.text: A West Indian curry of Indian origin, cooked with goat, pork, chicken or fish.

re-ermitage--le-20-decembre-fet-kaf.title: December 20, fèt kaf
re-ermitage--le-20-decembre-fet-kaf.text: A public holiday marking the abolition of slavery proclaimed in 1848; in Creole, it is called “fèt kaf” or “20 désamb.”

re-ermitage--le-rougail-saucisse.title: Rougail saucisse
re-ermitage--le-rougail-saucisse.text: Sausages cooked Creole style with tomatoes, onions and chili, served with rice and beans.

re-ermitage--le-maloya.title: Maloya
re-ermitage--le-maloya.text: Born in the time of slavery and carried by percussion (roulèr, kayamb), it has been UNESCO-listed since 2009.

tz-zanzibar-mnemba--mwaka-kogwa.title: Mwaka Kogwa
tz-zanzibar-mnemba--mwaka-kogwa.text: Shirazi New Year in Makunduchi, in July or August: a ritual fight, then a burning hut whose smoke is used to predict the year.

tz-zanzibar-mnemba--la-pizza-de-zanzibar.title: Zanzibar pizza
tz-zanzibar-mnemba--la-pizza-de-zanzibar.text: A kind of savory crêpe filled with beef, eggs and salad, eaten at the Forodhani night market in Stone Town.

tz-zanzibar-mnemba--jus-de-canne-et-lait.title: Sugarcane juice and coconut milk
tz-zanzibar-mnemba--jus-de-canne-et-lait.text: Stone Town’s sugarcane juice and fresh coconut milk are not to be missed.

tz-zanzibar-mnemba--une-tenue-pudique.title: Modest dress
tz-zanzibar-mnemba--une-tenue-pudique.text: Cover your legs and arms in town, and avoid public displays of affection; a bikini is fine on hotel beaches.

it-sardaigne-stintino--le-musee-de-la-to.title: Tonnara museum
it-sardaigne-stintino--le-musee-de-la-to.text: The former Saline tonnara fished tuna until the 1970s; the tuna fishermen’s museum has told its story since 2016.

it-sardaigne-stintino--la-bottarga-de-th.title: Tuna bottarga
it-sardaigne-stintino--la-bottarga-de-th.text: Dried tuna roe (bottarga) is among the dishes of the fishing tradition, along with garlic octopus and spiny lobster soup.

it-sardaigne-stintino--la-regate-des-goz.title: Gozzi regatta
it-sardaigne-stintino--la-regate-des-goz.text: Since 1983, Stintino has held a regatta for its gozzi, the fishermen’s traditional wooden sailboats.

it-sardaigne-stintino--la-fete-de-la-mad.title: Feast of the Madonna
it-sardaigne-stintino--la-fete-de-la-mad.text: September 8 is the day of Stintino’s patron saint, the Beata Vergine della Difesa.

gr-cephalonie-myrtos--les-serpents-de-la.title: The Virgin’s snakes
gr-cephalonie-myrtos--les-serpents-de-la.text: Before August 15, small harmless snakes, with a cross on their heads, enter the church of Markopoulo: a good omen.

gr-cephalonie-myrtos--la-kreatopita.title: Kreatopita
gr-cephalonie-myrtos--la-kreatopita.text: A meat pie, a farmhouse dish that is the specialty of Cephalonia.

gr-cephalonie-myrtos--le-miel-de-thym.title: Thyme honey
gr-cephalonie-myrtos--le-miel-de-thym.text: Cephalonia’s wild thyme honey is worth bringing home: its taste is truly distinctive.

gr-cephalonie-myrtos--le-robola.title: Robola
gr-cephalonie-myrtos--le-robola.text: A white grape grown mostly in Cephalonia, often ungrafted on the island’s limestone soils.

gr-cephalonie-myrtos--le-frappe-en-terra.title: Frappé on the terrace
gr-cephalonie-myrtos--le-frappe-en-terra.text: A frappé is a “ticket” to stay for hours on a terrace, like the Greeks do; also say hello in Greek.

fr-normandie-dieppe--la-marmite-dieppois.title: Marmite dieppoise
fr-normandie-dieppe--la-marmite-dieppois.text: A Dieppe specialty: a stew of fish and shellfish in white wine, with vegetables and herbs.

fr-normandie-dieppe--la-foire-aux-hareng.title: Herring and scallop fair
fr-normandie-dieppe--la-foire-aux-hareng.text: Every third weekend of November, grilled herring is eaten with a braised potato and melted salted butter.

fr-normandie-dieppe--le-marche-du-samedi.title: Saturday market
fr-normandie-dieppe--le-marche-du-samedi.text: On Saturdays, from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m., the food market fills Grande Rue, Place Nationale and Rue Saint-Jacques.

fr-normandie-dieppe--le-festival-de-cerf.title: Kite festival
fr-normandie-dieppe--le-festival-de-cerf.text: The international kite festival returns in September: the 2025 edition took place from the 13th to the 21st, after three years away.

fr-verdon-saintecroix--la-truffe-noire-d.title: Aups black truffle
fr-verdon-saintecroix--la-truffe-noire-d.text: Aups holds France’s third-largest black truffle market, in the morning, from late November to late February.

fr-verdon-saintecroix--l-huile-d-olive-e.title: Olive oil and lavender
fr-verdon-saintecroix--l-huile-d-olive-e.text: Around Moustiers, they produce Haute-Provence PDO olive oil, as well as honey and lavender essences.

fr-verdon-saintecroix--la-diane-de-moust.title: La Diane de Moustiers
fr-verdon-saintecroix--la-diane-de-moust.text: From August 31 to September 8, the Dianaïres wake the village with music at 5 a.m.; on the 8th, a dawn procession to the chapel.

fr-verdon-saintecroix--l-etoile-de-moust.title: The Moustiers star
fr-verdon-saintecroix--l-etoile-de-moust.text: A star hangs from a chain stretched between two cliffs above the village, according to the legend of the knight de Blacas.

fr-verdon-saintecroix--la-faience-de-mou.title: Moustiers faience
fr-verdon-saintecroix--la-faience-de-mou.text: The village was famed for its faience in the 17th and 18th centuries; the art revived in 1925 with Marcel Provence.

bz-belize-blue-hole--le-riz-aux-haricots.title: Rice and beans
bz-belize-blue-hole--le-riz-aux-haricots.text: A staple dish of the Kriols: rice simmered with beans and coconut milk, served with meat and a salad.

bz-belize-blue-hole--le-hudut-garifuna.title: Garifuna hudut
bz-belize-blue-hole--le-hudut-garifuna.text: Hudut is a Garifuna fish soup, prepared with or without coconut milk.

bz-belize-blue-hole--le-garifuna-settlem.title: Garifuna Settlement Day
bz-belize-blue-hole--le-garifuna-settlem.text: On November 19, a public holiday: parades, street music and traditional dances, especially in Dangriga.

bz-belize-blue-hole--le-st-george-s-caye.title: St George’s Caye Day
bz-belize-blue-hole--le-st-george-s-caye.text: On September 10, people mark the Battle of St George’s Caye, fought in 1798.

id-papua-rajaampat--le-papeda.title: Papeda
id-papua-rajaampat--le-papeda.text: A sago porridge from the Moluccas and the west coast of Papua, served with fish in a yellow broth.

id-papua-rajaampat--le-festival-pesona-r.title: Pesona Raja Ampat Festival
id-papua-rajaampat--le-festival-pesona-r.text: In October (15 to 18 in 2026), arts, local food and actions for the sea, in Raja Ampat. Admission is free.

id-papua-rajaampat--le-sasi.title: Sasi
id-papua-rajaampat--le-sasi.text: Residents ban the harvest of certain resources: from the closing ceremony to the reopening one.

id-papua-rajaampat--raja-ampat-les-quatr.title: Raja Ampat, the four kings
id-papua-rajaampat--raja-ampat-les-quatr.text: Raja Ampat means “four kings”: the name comes from a myth of seven eggs from which kings were born.

id-bali-nusapenida--le-babi-guling.title: Babi guling
id-bali-nusapenida--le-babi-guling.text: Suckling pig stuffed with spices and spit-roasted, often served with lawar rice; a specialty of Bali.

id-bali-nusapenida--les-canang-sari.title: Canang sari
id-bali-nusapenida--les-canang-sari.text: Every day, the Balinese place these small palm-leaf baskets as offerings, in temples and homes.

id-bali-nusapenida--galungan.title: Galungan
id-bali-nusapenida--galungan.text: Every 210 days, decorated bamboo poles (penjor) line the roads. Next dates: January 13 and August 11, 2027.

id-bali-nusapenida--le-basa-nosa.title: Basa Nosa
id-bali-nusapenida--le-basa-nosa.text: On the island, people speak a Balinese specific to Nusa Penida, which people from the rest of Bali do not understand.

id-lombok-gili--l-ayam-taliwang.title: Ayam Taliwang
id-lombok-gili--l-ayam-taliwang.text: Spicy, sweet grilled chicken with shrimp paste, born in Taliwang, near Mataram, the capital of Lombok.

id-lombok-gili--le-plecing-kangkung.title: Plecing kangkung
id-lombok-gili--le-plecing-kangkung.text: Blanched water spinach, served cold with a spicy sambal, often alongside ayam Taliwang.

id-lombok-gili--le-bau-nyale.title: Bau Nyale
id-lombok-gili--le-bau-nyale.text: In February or March, sea worms are gathered by hand after midnight on Seger beach, in memory of a princess.

id-lombok-gili--une-ile-sans-moteur.title: An island without engines
id-lombok-gili--une-ile-sans-moteur.text: Motor vehicles are banned by local decree: you get around by bicycle or cidomo, a small horse cart.

pf-tuamotu-tikehau--le-poisson-cru-au-la.title: Poisson cru au lait de coco
pf-tuamotu-tikehau--le-poisson-cru-au-la.text: The best-known dish of Polynesia: raw fish marinated in lime juice and coconut milk.

pf-tuamotu-tikehau--le-four-tahitien.title: Tahitian oven
pf-tuamotu-tikehau--le-four-tahitien.text: For festive meals, food is steamed in a pit lined with heated stones and covered with banana leaves.

pf-tuamotu-tikehau--le-heiva-i-tahiti.title: Heiva i Tahiti
pf-tuamotu-tikehau--le-heiva-i-tahiti.text: Each July, in Papeete, competing groups present traditional songs and dances, along with Polynesian sports.

pf-tuamotu-tikehau--les-parcs-a-poissons.title: Fish traps
pf-tuamotu-tikehau--les-parcs-a-poissons.text: The atoll practices traditional fishing with fish traps, near the Tuheiava pass.

th-surat-thani-kohtao--les-huitres-de-su.title: Surat Thani oysters
th-surat-thani-kohtao--les-huitres-de-su.text: The province is Thailand’s top oyster-farming area; they are eaten raw, with lime and chili.

th-surat-thani-kohtao--les-ufs-rouges.title: Red eggs
th-surat-thani-kohtao--les-ufs-rouges.text: Salted duck eggs, preserved in a mix of earth and salt: a specialty of Surat Thani province.

th-surat-thani-kohtao--le-chak-phra.title: Chak Phra
th-surat-thani-kohtao--le-chak-phra.text: Around October, nine days of processions of Buddha statues on land and water, with dugout canoe races.

th-surat-thani-kohtao--ko-tao-l-ile-aux-.title: Ko Tao, the turtle island
th-surat-thani-kohtao--ko-tao-l-ile-aux-.text: Ko Tao means “turtle island” in Thai.

th-surat-thani-kohtao--le-monogramme-du-.title: The king’s monogram
th-surat-thani-kohtao--le-monogramme-du-.text: Near Sairee beach, a rock bears the monogram left by King Chulalongkorn in 1899; it is still venerated.

us-floride-keylargo--la-key-lime-pie.title: Key lime pie
us-floride-keylargo--la-key-lime-pie.text: A Keys lime pie made with sweetened condensed milk; it has been Florida’s official pie since 2006.

us-floride-keylargo--la-mini-saison-de-l.title: Lobster mini-season
us-floride-keylargo--la-mini-saison-de-l.text: In July, the lobster mini-season opens for two days in the Keys (the 29th and 30th in 2026).

us-floride-keylargo--le-parc-pennekamp.title: Pennekamp Park
us-floride-keylargo--le-parc-pennekamp.text: Opened in 1963, it is the first underwater park in the United States; the Christ of the Abyss statue rests there in nearly 8 m of water.

us-floride-keylargo--les-conchs.title: The Conchs
us-floride-keylargo--les-conchs.text: Keys residents long called themselves “Conchs”; Key West even proclaimed its “Republic” on April 23, 1982.

es-galice-razo--le-polbo-a-feira.title: Polbo á feira
es-galice-razo--le-polbo-a-feira.text: Octopus boiled in a copper pot, then sprinkled with coarse salt and paprika and drizzled with olive oil.

es-galice-razo--la-queimada.title: Queimada
es-galice-razo--la-queimada.text: A punch of pomace brandy, sugar and peels, set aflame while reciting a spell to drive away evil spirits.

es-galice-razo--la-nuit-de-la-saint-jean.title: Saint John’s Eve
es-galice-razo--la-nuit-de-la-saint-jean.text: June 23 is witches’ night in Galicia: this is when queimada is mostly prepared.

es-galice-razo--la-morrina.title: Morriña
es-galice-razo--la-morrina.text: A Galician word for the melancholy felt far from the land where you were born.

es-galice-razo--la-feira-de-carballo.title: Carballo feira
es-galice-razo--la-feira-de-carballo.text: In Carballo, the farm produce market is held on Thursdays, and on the 2nd, 4th and 5th Sundays of the month.

co-sanandres--le-rondon.title: Rondón
co-sanandres--le-rondon.text: A stew of fish or sea snails, cassava, plantain and breadfruit, cooked in coconut milk.

co-sanandres--la-veda-du-crabe-noir.title: Black crab closed season
co-sanandres--la-veda-du-crabe-noir.text: Every year, from April 1 to July 31, hunting the black crab is banned, because the species is threatened.

co-sanandres--le-creole-raizal.title: Raizal Creole
co-sanandres--le-creole-raizal.text: The Raizals, the islands’ Afro-Caribbean community, speak the Creole of San Andrés and Providencia, plus Spanish and English.

nz-coromandel-cathedralcove--te-whanganu.title: Te Whanganui-A-Hei
nz-coromandel-cathedralcove--te-whanganu.text: The Maori name of the place means “the great bay of Hei,” after a tohunga of the Te Arawa canoe.

nz-coromandel-cathedralcove--le-hangi.title: Hāngī
nz-coromandel-cathedralcove--le-hangi.text: Maori earth-oven cooking: meat, vegetables and seafood cook on hot stones buried in the ground.

nz-coromandel-cathedralcove--le-whitiang.title: Whitianga Oceans Festival
nz-coromandel-cathedralcove--le-whitiang.text: Every September, Whitianga celebrates Coromandel seafood (September 14 in 2024).

nz-coromandel-cathedralcove--matariki.title: Matariki
nz-coromandel-cathedralcove--matariki.text: Maori New Year, at the rising of the Pleiades, a public holiday since 2022: July 10, 2026, then June 25, 2027.

nz-coromandel-cathedralcove--hot-water-b.title: Hot Water Beach
nz-coromandel-cathedralcove--hot-water-b.text: For two hours around low tide, you dig in the sand to let hot water seep up, up to 64 °C.

nl-la-haye-scheveningen--le-hareng-nouve.title: Hollandse Nieuwe
nl-la-haye-scheveningen--le-hareng-nouve.text: Lightly salted raw herring, eaten holding it by the tail, often with raw onions.

nl-la-haye-scheveningen--vlaggetjesdag.title: Vlaggetjesdag
nl-la-haye-scheveningen--vlaggetjesdag.text: On the third Saturday of June, the harbor is decked with flags for the herring season, with the auction of the first small barrel.

nl-la-haye-scheveningen--le-plongeon-du-.title: New Year’s Dive
nl-la-haye-scheveningen--le-plongeon-du-.text: On January 1, a polar dip in the sea: 50,000 people took part in 2016.

nl-la-haye-scheveningen--le-kurhaus.title: Kurhaus
nl-la-haye-scheveningen--le-kurhaus.text: The Kurhaus, a hotel in Scheveningen, opened its doors in 1886.

eg-mer-rouge-elgouna--le-koshari.title: Koshari
eg-mer-rouge-elgouna--le-koshari.text: A mix of rice, lentils and macaroni, sold on the street; some see it as Egypt’s national dish.

eg-mer-rouge-elgouna--le-the.title: Tea
eg-mer-rouge-elgouna--le-the.text: Tea is Egypt’s national drink, often served with mint.

eg-mer-rouge-elgouna--le-festival-du-fil.title: El Gouna Film Festival
eg-mer-rouge-elgouna--le-festival-du-fil.text: Every October, the resort hosts a film festival founded in 2017.

eg-mer-rouge-elgouna--al-gouna-la-lagune.title: Al-Gouna, the lagoon
eg-mer-rouge-elgouna--al-gouna-la-lagune.text: El Gouna’s Arabic name means “the lagoon”: the town spreads over 20 islands surrounded by lagoons.

ky-grandcayman-stingray--le-lambi.title: Conch
ky-grandcayman-stingray--le-lambi.text: Conch is prepared marinated, in salad, in chowder or in stew; it has long been a staple dish of the Caymans.

ky-grandcayman-stingray--la-pirates-week.title: Pirates Week
ky-grandcayman-stingray--la-pirates-week.text: In November, reenactments of pirate invasions, a big cultural parade and a cardboard boat race (November 8 to 22 in 2025).

ky-grandcayman-stingray--les-raies-de-st.title: The Stingray City rays
ky-grandcayman-stingray--les-raies-de-st.text: The rays are said to have gathered when fishermen cleaned their catch in the shallows, then learned to associate boat engines with food.

ve-losroques--l-arepa.title: Arepa
ve-losroques--l-arepa.text: The arepa, a corn cake, is eaten at any hour in Venezuela; the “reina pepiada” is filled with chicken, avocado and mayonnaise.

ve-losroques--le-festival-de-la-langosta.title: Festival de la Langosta
ve-losroques--le-festival-de-la-langosta.text: In November, when the fishing season opens, the archipelago celebrates the spiny lobster, one of its emblematic animals.

ve-losroques--la-virgen-del-valle.title: Virgen del Valle
ve-losroques--la-virgen-del-valle.text: In the second week of September, a boat procession leaves Crasquí for Gran Roque: the Virgin protects the fishermen.

ve-losroques--gran-roque.title: Gran Roque
ve-losroques--gran-roque.text: Almost all residents live in Gran Roque, a small village of seven sand streets.

fj-vitilevu-beqa--le-kokoda.title: Kokoda
fj-vitilevu-beqa--le-kokoda.text: Raw fish marinated in lime and coconut milk, with diced vegetables (cucumber, tomato, onion).

fj-vitilevu-beqa--le-lovo.title: Lovo
fj-vitilevu-beqa--le-lovo.text: The lovo is the Fijian earth oven: heated stones in a pit, food covered with earth, for big occasions.

fj-vitilevu-beqa--la-marche-sur-le-feu.title: Fire walking
fj-vitilevu-beqa--la-marche-sur-le-feu.text: Five Beqa villages are renowned for fire walking (vilavilairevo), already a tourist attraction in 1902.

fj-vitilevu-beqa--le-hibiscus-festival.title: Hibiscus Festival
fj-vitilevu-beqa--le-hibiscus-festival.text: In late August and early September, Suva elects queens and offers cultural programs (August 31 to September 7 in 2024).

to-vavau--la-cuisine-traditionnelle.title: Traditional cuisine
to-vavau--la-cuisine-traditionnelle.text: The traditional diet is based on taro, yam, banana, coconut and fish cooked in leaves.

to-vavau--le-dimanche-tongien.title: Tongan Sunday
to-vavau--le-dimanche-tongien.text: The Sabbath is written into the constitution: on Sundays, shops and entertainment stop.

to-vavau--le-four-en-terre-umu.title: The umu earth oven
to-vavau--le-four-en-terre-umu.text: In the past, the big midday meal was cooked in an earth oven; wedding and funeral pork was also prepared there.

to-vavau--le-port-de-neiafu.title: Neiafu harbor
to-vavau--le-port-de-neiafu.text: Neiafu, capital of Vavaʻu, is a sheltered port; from May to October, it welcomes sailboats from around the world.

yt-mayotte-ngouja--le-mataba.title: Mataba
yt-mayotte-ngouja--le-mataba.text: Cassava leaves simmered in coconut milk, a dish that takes long to prepare and is served mostly at ceremonies.

yt-mayotte-ngouja--la-chahoula-ya-nadzi.title: Chahoula ya nadzi
yt-mayotte-ngouja--la-chahoula-ya-nadzi.text: Rice cooked in water or coconut milk, a must at ceremonies (circumcision, debbah, maoulida) and big family meals.

yt-mayotte-ngouja--le-maoulida-shengue.title: Maoulida shengué
yt-mayotte-ngouja--le-maoulida-shengue.text: A traditional art mixing song, dance and choreography, on the national intangible cultural heritage list since June 2022.

yt-mayotte-ngouja--la-salouva.title: Salouva
yt-mayotte-ngouja--la-salouva.text: Women often wear the salouva, a colorful garment; men wear white cotton outfits.

yt-mayotte-ngouja--le-kibushi.title: Kibushi
yt-mayotte-ngouja--le-kibushi.text: A language of Malagasy origin, Kibushi is the mother tongue of about 30% of Mayotte’s residents.

no-jaeren-borestranda--le-j-dersylte.title: Jædersylte
no-jaeren-borestranda--le-j-dersylte.text: A local product of Jæren: minced meat and fat, then canned.

no-jaeren-borestranda--gladmat.title: Gladmat
no-jaeren-borestranda--gladmat.text: In late June, in Stavanger, Norway’s biggest food festival: local producers on the harbor (June 23 to 26, 2027).

no-jaeren-borestranda--la-j-rdagen.title: Jærdagen
no-jaeren-borestranda--la-j-rdagen.text: On the last weekend of May, Bryne celebrates Jærdagen, its town festival.

no-jaeren-borestranda--le-droit-d-acces-.title: Right of access to nature
no-jaeren-borestranda--le-droit-d-acces-.text: Anyone may roam uncultivated land, camp at least 150 m from a house and pick berries.

no-jaeren-borestranda--le-j-rsk.title: Jærsk
no-jaeren-borestranda--le-j-rsk.text: People speak Jærsk there, a southwestern Norwegian dialect, mainly in Hå, Time and Klepp.

se-bohuslan-kosterhavet--plateaux-de-fru.title: Seafood platters and shrimp parties
se-bohuslan-kosterhavet--plateaux-de-fru.text: In Strömstad, restaurants serve seafood platters and shrimp parties during Smaka på Bohuslän.

se-bohuslan-kosterhavet--l-ouverture-de-.title: Lobster fishing opening
se-bohuslan-kosterhavet--l-ouverture-de-.text: On the first Monday after September 20, at 7 a.m. sharp, lobster fishing opens; it runs until November 30.

se-bohuslan-kosterhavet--smaka-pa-bohusl.title: Smaka på Bohuslän
se-bohuslan-kosterhavet--smaka-pa-bohusl.text: In early October, Strömstad celebrates the flavors of Bohuslän: seafood, lobster fishing, farm visits (October 2 to 11).

se-bohuslan-kosterhavet--l-allemansratte.title: Allemansrätten
se-bohuslan-kosterhavet--l-allemansratte.text: The public right of access lets you walk, camp for a night or two and pick berries and mushrooms outside cultivated land.

se-bohuslan-kosterhavet--les-huitres-du-.title: The landowner’s oysters
se-bohuslan-kosterhavet--les-huitres-du-.text: Oysters belong to the landowner: you cannot gather them wherever you like.

dk-jutland-hvidesande--les-limandes-sech.title: Dried dabs
dk-jutland-hvidesande--les-limandes-sech.text: Dried dabs are Hvide Sande’s local treat, tasted for free at the Æ Dabs festival.

dk-jutland-hvidesande--dabs-day.title: Æ Dabs Day
dk-jutland-hvidesande--dabs-day.text: On Ascension Day, Metheasvej street is closed to taste dried dabs, with music and shops open.

dk-jutland-hvidesande--le-festival-du-ha.title: Herring festival
dk-jutland-hvidesande--le-festival-du-ha.text: Late April: smoked herring under a tent, fishing contests and music (April 23 to 25, 2027).

dk-jutland-hvidesande--waterz.title: Waterz
dk-jutland-hvidesande--waterz.text: In early September, Scandinavia’s biggest water sports festival: windsurfing, kitesurfing, surfing, SUP (September 3 and 4, 2027).

dk-jutland-hvidesande--la-criee-du-diman.title: Sunday auction
dk-jutland-hvidesande--la-criee-du-diman.text: Every Sunday in July and August, and one Sunday in October, you can bid on the day’s catch at the fish auction.

ie-sligo-easkey--les-produits-de-sligo.title: Sligo produce
ie-sligo-easkey--les-produits-de-sligo.text: County Sligo highlights Lissadell oysters, wild Mullaghmore lobster and Knocknarea honey.

ie-sligo-easkey--les-bains-d-algues.title: Seaweed baths
ie-sligo-easkey--les-bains-d-algues.text: Seaweed baths, which appeared in the Victorian era, survive in Enniscrone: the Kilcullen house dates from 1912.

ie-sligo-easkey--le-poll-gorm.title: Poll Gorm
ie-sligo-easkey--le-poll-gorm.text: A natural saltwater pool whose wall was built in 1966 by four locals; local children learn to swim there.

ie-sligo-easkey--iascaigh.title: Iascaigh
ie-sligo-easkey--iascaigh.text: Iascaigh, the Irish name of Easkey, means “rich in fish.”

ec-galapagos-puntacarola--le-ceviche-de-.title: Canchalagua ceviche
ec-galapagos-puntacarola--le-ceviche-de-.text: Canchalagua ceviche is especially typical of San Cristóbal, the easternmost island of the archipelago.

ec-galapagos-puntacarola--la-cantonisati.title: Cantonization
ec-galapagos-puntacarola--la-cantonisati.text: On February 18, Puerto Baquerizo Moreno celebrates cantonization, its major festival.

ec-galapagos-puntacarola--la-distance-av.title: Distance from animals
ec-galapagos-puntacarola--la-distance-av.text: In the national park, stay at least 2 m from animals, even if they approach, and don’t feed them or leave the trails.

ec-galapagos-puntacarola--la-loberia.title: La Lobería
ec-galapagos-puntacarola--la-loberia.text: This sea lion colony is ten minutes by bus from Puerto Baquerizo Moreno.

ec-galapagos-puntacarola--la-statue-de-d.title: Darwin statue
ec-galapagos-puntacarola--la-statue-de-d.text: A statue marks the spot where Darwin first landed in the Galápagos, on September 16, 1835.

vi-saintjohn-trunkbay--le-fungi.title: Fungi
vi-saintjohn-trunkbay--le-fungi.text: Cornmeal polenta with okra, served with boiled fish or salt cod.

vi-saintjohn-trunkbay--le-kallaloo.title: Kallaloo
vi-saintjohn-trunkbay--le-kallaloo.text: A soup of callaloo leaves, sometimes replaced by spinach.

vi-saintjohn-trunkbay--la-st-john-celebr.title: St. John Celebration
vi-saintjohn-trunkbay--la-st-john-celebr.text: June 14 to July 4, 2026: Fourth of July parade, steel bands, cooking contests and fireworks over Cruz Bay.

vi-saintjohn-trunkbay--le-j-ouvert.title: J’ouvert
vi-saintjohn-trunkbay--le-j-ouvert.text: J’ouvert (“daybreak”): at dawn, people dance to soca and calypso, covered in mud, powder and paint.

vi-saintjohn-trunkbay--le-sentier-sous-m.title: Underwater trail
vi-saintjohn-trunkbay--le-sentier-sous-m.text: The trail runs along Trunk Bay Cay for about 90 m (300 feet), and its plaques help beginners recognize marine life.

fr-paysbasque-cotebasque--le-gateau-basq.title: Gâteau basque
fr-paysbasque-cotebasque--le-gateau-basq.text: Shortcrust pastry filled with black cherries or custard: the “house biscuit” (etxeko biskotxa), served on feast days.

fr-paysbasque-cotebasque--le-rocher-de-l.title: Rocher de la Vierge
fr-paysbasque-cotebasque--le-rocher-de-l.text: A promontory shaped like a ship’s hull, topped by a statue of the Virgin: the emblem of Biarritz, with views over the bay and the Pyrenees.

fr-paysbasque-cotebasque--le-ttoro-de-sa.title: Ttoro of Saint-Jean-de-Luz
fr-paysbasque-cotebasque--le-ttoro-de-sa.text: The fishermen’s soup of Saint-Jean-de-Luz, Ciboure and Socoa, originally made from the unsold fish of the day: hake, shellfish and clams.

fr-paysbasque-cotebasque--le-macaron-de-.title: Macaron of Saint-Jean-de-Luz
fr-paysbasque-cotebasque--le-macaron-de-.text: A pastry cook named Adam is said to have offered them to Louis XIV for his wedding in 1660, and his descendants keep the tradition alive.

fr-paysbasque-cotebasque--la-maison-de-l.title: Maison de l’Infante
fr-paysbasque-cotebasque--la-maison-de-l.text: A pink brick and stone house (about 1640) on the harbour, where the Infanta Maria Theresa was received to marry Louis XIV in 1660.

fr-gironde-lacanau--le-lacanau-pro.title: Lacanau Pro
fr-gironde-lacanau--le-lacanau-pro.text: France’s oldest professional surf competition, born in 1979 at the Lacanau Surf Club, is held every year in August.

fr-gironde-lacanau--le-cannele.title: Cannelé
fr-gironde-lacanau--le-cannele.text: A small Bordeaux cake with rum and vanilla, baked in a fluted mould, originally copper, that gives it a thin caramelised crust.

fr-gironde-lacanau--le-lac-de-lacanau.title: Lake Lacanau
fr-gironde-lacanau--le-lac-de-lacanau.text: At nearly 2,000 hectares, one of the big lakes of the Landes coast; the Canal des Étangs links it to Hourtin in the north and Arcachon Bay in the south.

fr-gironde-lacanau--le-45e-parallele.title: The 45th parallel
fr-gironde-lacanau--le-45e-parallele.text: Lacanau lies on the 45th parallel north: halfway between the North Pole and the equator, about 5,000 km from each.

fr-morbihan-belleile--les-aiguilles-de-p.title: Aiguilles de Port-Coton
fr-morbihan-belleile--les-aiguilles-de-p.text: These rocks on the wild coast are named after the foam which, in heavy swell, looks like a cotton veil. Monet painted them in 1886.

fr-morbihan-belleile--les-acadiens-de-be.title: The Acadians of Belle-Île
fr-morbihan-belleile--les-acadiens-de-be.text: From 1765, 78 Acadian families driven out in the “Great Upheaval” of 1755 settled on the island.

fr-morbihan-belleile--l-agneau-du-large.title: Agneau du large
fr-morbihan-belleile--l-agneau-du-large.text: The “Agneau du large” label, created in 1994, certifies a lamb born on the island that has spent at least 60 days at pasture.

fr-morbihan-belleile--le-bois-du-genie.title: Bois du Génie
fr-morbihan-belleile--le-bois-du-genie.text: This wood was planted around Vauban’s fortifications to hide and protect them; its name comes from the army engineers who decided it.

fr-bretagne-saintmalo--la-route-du-rhum.title: Route du Rhum
fr-bretagne-saintmalo--la-route-du-rhum.text: A solo race between Saint-Malo and Guadeloupe, every four years since 1978, from late October to early November.

fr-bretagne-saintmalo--le-grand-be.title: Grand Bé
fr-bretagne-saintmalo--le-grand-be.text: An uninhabited island below the ramparts, reached on foot at low tide: Chateaubriand is buried there, as he wished.

fr-bretagne-saintmalo--la-cite-des-corsa.title: The city of privateers
fr-bretagne-saintmalo--la-cite-des-corsa.text: Once a city of privateers, Saint-Malo gave birth to captains such as Duguay-Trouin and Surcouf; its people are the Malouins.

fr-bretagne-saintmalo--les-huitres-plate.title: Flat oysters of Cancale
fr-bretagne-saintmalo--les-huitres-plate.text: Fifteen kilometres to the east, Cancale is known for its wild flat oysters, from natural deep-water beds.

fr-normandie-etretat--les-falaises-et-le.title: Cliffs and the three arches
fr-normandie-etretat--les-falaises-et-le.text: Chalk cliffs pierced by three arches: Porte d’Amont, Porte d’Aval and the Manneporte, said to have been first carved by an underground river.

fr-normandie-etretat--l-aiguille-creuse.title: L’Aiguille creuse
fr-normandie-etretat--l-aiguille-creuse.text: Maurice Leblanc, who lived in Étretat, made the Needle the hideout of Arsène Lupin in his novel “L’Aiguille creuse” (1909).

fr-normandie-etretat--les-peintres-d-etr.title: Painters of Étretat
fr-normandie-etretat--les-peintres-d-etr.text: Monet, Courbet, Boudin and Marquet painted the character of the place, by turns calm or fierce, and made its reputation.

fr-normandie-etretat--les-fetes-d-offenb.title: Offenbach and Maupassant parties
fr-normandie-etretat--les-fetes-d-offenb.text: In the 19th century, artists such as Offenbach and Maupassant threw parties here for their friends, as the resort became fashionable.

fr-provence-calanques--la-bouillabaisse.title: Bouillabaisse
fr-provence-calanques--la-bouillabaisse.text: Marseille’s emblematic fish soup, served with garlic-rubbed croutons spread with rouille, pieces of fish and potatoes.

fr-provence-calanques--le-parc-national-.title: Calanques National Park
fr-provence-calanques--le-parc-national-.text: Created in April 2012, it is the first peri-urban national park in Europe and the third in the world.

fr-provence-calanques--calanque.title: Calanque
fr-provence-calanques--calanque.text: The word comes from the Provençal calanco: a valley carved by a river, then flooded by the sea.

fr-provence-calanques--le-vin-de-cassis.title: Cassis wine
fr-provence-calanques--le-vin-de-cassis.text: Cassis is an appellation wine, the first AOC recognised in Provence, in 1936; it comes in white and rosé.

fr-var-pampelonne--la-tarte-tropezienne.title: Tarte tropézienne
fr-var-pampelonne--la-tarte-tropezienne.text: A brioche split in two and filled with custard and butter cream; pastry cook Alexandre Micka’s original recipe is kept secret.

fr-var-pampelonne--la-bravade-de-mai.title: Bravade of May
fr-var-pampelonne--la-bravade-de-mai.text: On 16 May the mayor hands the pike to the Town Captain elected on Easter Monday; sailors and musketeers fire salvoes, and weapons are blessed.

fr-var-pampelonne--la-bravade-du-15-juin.title: Bravade of 15 June
fr-var-pampelonne--la-bravade-du-15-juin.text: On 15 June 1637 the people of Saint-Tropez defeated 21 Spanish galleys, a victory celebrated ever since with a bravade.

fr-var-pampelonne--la-plage-de-pampelonn.title: Pampelonne beach
fr-var-pampelonne--la-plage-de-pampelonn.text: A 4.5 km sandy beach covering 27 hectares, in the commune of Ramatuelle, not Saint-Tropez, on the state’s public maritime domain.

gp-basseterre-cousteau--la-reserve-coust.title: Cousteau Reserve
gp-basseterre-cousteau--la-reserve-coust.text: A marine reserve of about 400 hectares around the Pigeon islets, off Malendure beach: it protects the seabed and limits fishing.

gp-basseterre-cousteau--le-gwoka.title: Gwoka
gp-basseterre-cousteau--le-gwoka.text: Guadeloupean music played mostly on “ka” drums: the largest keeps the rhythm, the smallest follows the dancers and singers.

gp-basseterre-cousteau--le-carnaval-de-g.title: Guadeloupe carnival
gp-basseterre-cousteau--le-carnaval-de-g.text: From January to Ash Wednesday: a grand parade in Pointe-à-Pitre on Fat Sunday, then Vaval, king of the carnival, is burned on the last day.

gp-basseterre-cousteau--le-ti-punch.title: Ti’ punch
gp-basseterre-cousteau--le-ti-punch.text: Rum, lime and cane syrup: this little cocktail is said to have been born on Marie-Galante and is part of social life in the Antilles.

mq-anses-darlet-dufour--deux-anses-deux-.title: Two coves, two sands
mq-anses-darlet-dufour--deux-anses-deux-.text: Anse Dufour has white sand, its neighbour Anse Noire black volcanic sand, the only black sand beach in the south of Martinique.

mq-anses-darlet-dufour--l-eglise-saint-h.title: Saint-Henri church
mq-anses-darlet-dufour--l-eglise-saint-h.text: Beside the beach, one of Martinique’s most beautiful spots thanks to its line-up with the jetty; restored in 2008 after Hurricane Dean.

mq-anses-darlet-dufour--le-feroce-d-avoc.title: Féroce d’avocat
mq-anses-darlet-dufour--le-feroce-d-avoc.text: Mashed avocado with shredded salt cod and chilli: its name comes from the chilli. Mostly served as an aperitif or starter.

mq-anses-darlet-dufour--le-madras.title: Madras
mq-anses-darlet-dufour--le-madras.text: A checked cloth from Madras, in India, turned into Creole headwraps in the Antilles; Joséphine de Beauharnais is said to have started the fashion.

pt-leiria-nazare--les-sept-jupons.title: The seven petticoats
pt-leiria-nazare--les-sept-jupons.text: Seven skirts, so tradition says. One disputed explanation: waiting for the fishermen, the women sheltered from the spray under the top ones.

pt-leiria-nazare--la-fete-de-notre-dame-.title: Feast of Our Lady of Nazaré
pt-leiria-nazare--la-fete-de-notre-dame-.text: 8 September, a public holiday, falls during ten days of festivities: processions, fireworks, dancing, a fair and bullfights.

pt-leiria-nazare--le-funiculaire-du-siti.title: Sítio funicular
pt-leiria-nazare--le-funiculaire-du-siti.text: Three districts: Praia, along the beach, the Sítio, the old village on the cliff, and Pederneira; a funicular links the beach to the Sítio.

pt-leiria-nazare--la-plus-grosse-vague-s.title: Biggest wave surfed
pt-leiria-nazare--la-plus-grosse-vague-s.text: In 2020, Germany’s Sebastian Steudtner surfed a wave measured at 26.2 metres at Nazaré, the biggest ever surfed.

pt-peniche--les-dentelles-aux-fuseaux.title: Bobbin lace
pt-peniche--les-dentelles-aux-fuseaux.text: Peniche lace (rendas de bilros) won a silver medal at the international exhibitions of Paris and London in 1851.

pt-peniche--la-forteresse-de-peniche.title: Peniche fortress
pt-peniche--la-forteresse-de-peniche.text: This fortress served as a political prison under the Estado Novo; today it houses a museum on the resistance to that regime.

pt-peniche--un-grand-port-de-peche.title: A major fishing port
pt-peniche--un-grand-port-de-peche.text: One of Portugal’s major fishing ports, with shipyards and fish canneries; the town is partly ringed by 16th-century ramparts.

pt-peniche--l-archipel-des-berlengas.title: Berlengas archipelago
pt-peniche--l-archipel-des-berlengas.text: Off Peniche, lead anchor bars (2.5 m, 420 kg) have been found; one dates from the late 5th century BC.

pt-madere-jardimdomar--la-poncha.title: Poncha
pt-madere-jardimdomar--la-poncha.text: A Madeiran drink: cane spirit, honey, lemon or orange. Its name comes from a word for “five”, like the original ingredients.

pt-madere-jardimdomar--le-bolo-do-caco.title: Bolo do caco
pt-madere-jardimdomar--le-bolo-do-caco.text: A flat round bread baked on a basalt slab, the “caco”, in Madeira and Porto Santo; served with garlic butter or as a sandwich.

pt-madere-jardimdomar--les-malasadas-du-.title: Carnival malasadas
pt-madere-jardimdomar--les-malasadas-du-.text: A sweet treat of the island, eaten mostly during Madeira’s carnival.

pt-madere-jardimdomar--le-vin-de-madere.title: Madeira wine
pt-madere-jardimdomar--le-vin-de-madere.text: English merchants settled in Funchal from the 17th century and controlled the wine trade; the Blandy’s house dates from 1811.

es-paysbasque-guipuzcoa-biscaye--la-tamb.title: Tamborrada
es-paysbasque-guipuzcoa-biscaye--la-tamb.text: On 20 January in San Sebastián the flag is raised at midnight and the festival lasts 24 hours: cooks and soldiers parade drumming.

es-paysbasque-guipuzcoa-biscaye--les-pin.title: Pintxos
es-paysbasque-guipuzcoa-biscaye--les-pin.text: Small snacks to skewer (“pintxo” means thorn), eaten in bars and taverns; hugely popular all over the Basque Country.

es-paysbasque-guipuzcoa-biscaye--le-txak.title: Getaria txakoli
es-paysbasque-guipuzcoa-biscaye--le-txak.text: A very pale white wine, yellow to green, made around Getaria, Zarautz and Aia: the first txakoli to receive an appellation.

es-paysbasque-guipuzcoa-biscaye--l-estua.title: Urdaibai estuary
es-paysbasque-guipuzcoa-biscaye--l-estua.text: The Mundaka estuary, also called the Gernika estuary, is a 220 km² biosphere reserve on the Basque coast.

es-andalousie-tarifa--levante-et-ponient.title: Levante and Poniente
es-andalousie-tarifa--levante-et-ponient.text: The Strait of Gibraltar at Tarifa speeds up the east (Levante) and west (Poniente) winds: an average of over 10 knots.

es-andalousie-tarifa--le-chateau-de-guzm.title: Guzmán Castle
es-andalousie-tarifa--le-chateau-de-guzm.text: Well preserved near the port, it was ordered around 960 by Caliph Abd al-Rahman III; the 13th-century Guzmán el Bueno tower is attached.

es-andalousie-tarifa--la-peche-a-l-almad.title: Almadraba tuna fishing
es-andalousie-tarifa--la-peche-a-l-almad.text: Ancient net traps for bluefin tuna, which enters the Mediterranean from February to July; Tarifa is one of the almadraba ports.

es-andalousie-tarifa--baelo-claudia.title: Baelo Claudia
es-andalousie-tarifa--baelo-claudia.text: At Bolonia, 22 km from Tarifa, the Roman town lived off tuna, salting and garum; Emperor Claudius made it a municipium.

es-canaries-lanzarote--les-papas-arrugad.title: Papas arrugadas
es-canaries-lanzarote--les-papas-arrugad.text: Boiled “wrinkled” potatoes served with mojo rojo; you eat them without cutlery, straight from the shared dishes.

es-canaries-lanzarote--le-mojo.title: Mojo
es-canaries-lanzarote--le-mojo.text: A sauce of olive oil, garlic, chilli and spices, born in the Canaries: green (mojo verde), red (mojo rojo) or very spicy (mojo picón).

es-canaries-lanzarote--les-vignes-de-la-.title: Vines of La Geria
es-canaries-lanzarote--les-vignes-de-la-.text: At La Geria, lava from the 1730 Timanfaya eruption covers the ground: each vine is rooted down to the old soil, sheltered from the wind by a wall, the zoco.

es-canaries-lanzarote--cesar-manrique.title: César Manrique
es-canaries-lanzarote--cesar-manrique.text: The local artist César Manrique (born 1919) transformed the volcanic caves of Jameos del Agua in the 1970s, respecting nature.

gb-cornwall-fistral--le-cornish-pasty.title: Cornish pasty
gb-cornwall-fistral--le-cornish-pasty.text: A crimped pastry parcel filled with beef, potato, swede and onion; it has had protected geographical status in Europe since 2011.

gb-cornwall-fistral--les-boardmasters.title: Boardmasters
gb-cornwall-fistral--les-boardmasters.text: Music, surf and skate in Newquay, about five days over the second weekend of August; a surf contest since 1981, with music since 2005.

gb-cornwall-fistral--le-huer-s-hut.title: Huer’s Hut
gb-cornwall-fistral--le-huer-s-hut.text: A small stone building, perhaps 14th century, a lookout in the 16th: the “huer” signalled the sardines and guided the fishermen to them.

gb-cornwall-fistral--le-saffron-bun.title: Saffron bun
gb-cornwall-fistral--le-saffron-bun.text: A sweet bun with saffron, raisins and spices, called a “revel bun” in Cornwall; baked in a large tin, it becomes a “saffron cake”.

ie-clare-lahinch--leath-inse.title: Leath Inse
ie-clare-lahinch--leath-inse.text: Lahinch comes from the Irish Leath Inse, “half-island” or “peninsula”.

ie-clare-lahinch--le-golf-sur-les-dunes.title: Golf on the dunes
ie-clare-lahinch--le-golf-sur-les-dunes.text: Lahinch Golf Club, founded in 1892, is a links course; in 2024 its Old Course is ranked 27th best golf course in the world by Golf Digest.

ie-clare-lahinch--les-falaises-de-moher.title: Cliffs of Moher
ie-clare-lahinch--les-falaises-de-moher.text: In the same County Clare, they run for about 14 km and rise to 214 metres, just north of O’Brien’s Tower.

ie-clare-lahinch--l-ecole-de-musique-wil.title: Willie Clancy Summer School
ie-clare-lahinch--l-ecole-de-musique-wil.text: At Milltown Malbay, the world’s largest summer school of traditional music: nearly a thousand students, in early July.

it-campanie-capri--la-fete-de-san-costan.title: Feast of San Costanzo
it-campanie-capri--la-fete-de-san-costan.text: On 14 May the town of Capri celebrates San Costanzo, its patron saint; Anacapri celebrates its own, Sant’Antonio, on 13 June.

it-campanie-capri--l-insalata-caprese.title: Insalata caprese
it-campanie-capri--l-insalata-caprese.text: Mozzarella, tomatoes and basil with olive oil; its name points to Capri, where it is thought to have been born. Famous in the 1950s.

it-campanie-capri--la-grotte-bleue.title: Blue Grotto
it-campanie-capri--la-grotte-bleue.text: A sea cave: sunlight enters through an underwater opening and makes the water glow bright blue; it runs 50 m into the cliff.

it-campanie-capri--le-limoncello.title: Limoncello
it-campanie-capri--le-limoncello.text: A lemon-zest liqueur made mostly around the Gulf of Naples; served well chilled as a digestif.

gr-cyclades-milos--la-venus-de-milo.title: Venus de Milo
gr-cyclades-milos--la-venus-de-milo.text: The statue was found in 1820 on the island of Milos and has been on show at the Louvre in Paris since 1821.

gr-cyclades-milos--l-obsidienne-de-milos.title: Obsidian of Milos
gr-cyclades-milos--l-obsidienne-de-milos.text: Since the Early Helladic period, the island sold obsidian to much of mainland Greece, and to Cyprus, Crete and Egypt.

gr-cyclades-milos--phylakopi.title: Phylakopi
gr-cyclades-milos--phylakopi.text: One of the most important sites of the Aegean world for the Early Bronze Age; Milos was a major economic centre of the Minoans.

gr-cyclades-milos--les-sculptures-de-mil.title: Sculptures of Milos
gr-cyclades-milos--les-sculptures-de-mil.text: The island gave us the Poseidon of Milos (in Athens), the Asclepius of Milos (British Museum) and an Archaic Apollo, besides the Venus.

gr-crete-balos--le-dakos.title: Dakos
gr-crete-balos--le-dakos.text: A Cretan salad: soaked hard bread (paximadi), tomatoes, feta or mizithra, herbs such as oregano; olives and capers are often added.

gr-crete-balos--la-tsikoudia.title: Tsikoudia
gr-crete-balos--la-tsikoudia.text: A grape-pomace spirit from Crete, 40 to 65% alcohol; in eastern Crete it is often called raki.

gr-crete-balos--le-paximadi.title: Paximadi
gr-crete-balos--le-paximadi.text: A hard bread of wholemeal wheat, chickpea or barley, like a rusk; often served at breakfast with jam or cheese.

gr-crete-balos--imeri-gramvousa.title: Imeri Gramvousa
gr-crete-balos--imeri-gramvousa.text: The neighbouring island keeps a Venetian fort and the buildings of Cretan insurgents who lived there as pirates during the Greek War of Independence.

hr-dalmatie-brac--le-zlatni-rat.title: Zlatni Rat
hr-dalmatie-brac--le-zlatni-rat.text: A spit of white pebbles 2 km west of the port of Bol. Its tip shifts with wind and currents, sometimes within a few hours.

hr-dalmatie-brac--la-pierre-blanche-de-b.title: White stone of Brač
hr-dalmatie-brac--la-pierre-blanche-de-b.text: The island’s white limestone, quarried for thousands of years, built Diocletian’s Palace in Split (295 to 305) and the Vimy Memorial.

hr-dalmatie-brac--la-grotte-de-kopacina.title: Kopačina cave
hr-dalmatie-brac--la-grotte-de-kopacina.text: Between Supetar and Donji Humac, a cave with human traces from the 12th millennium BC, among the oldest in Dalmatia.

hr-dalmatie-brac--l-huile-d-olive-de-bra.title: Olive oil of Brač
hr-dalmatie-brac--l-huile-d-olive-de-bra.text: Olives have been grown on the island since Roman times, and its oil now has a protected designation of origin.

ma-souss-agadir-taghazout--l-huile-d-arg.title: Argan oil
ma-souss-agadir-taghazout--l-huile-d-arg.text: In Morocco, you dip bread in it at breakfast or pour some on couscous; the argan tree comes from Morocco and south-west Algeria.

ma-souss-agadir-taghazout--l-amlou.title: Amlou
ma-souss-agadir-taghazout--l-amlou.text: A spread of crushed roasted almonds, honey and argan oil, served at breakfast or teatime with crêpes and pastries.

ma-souss-agadir-taghazout--le-the-a-la-m.title: Mint tea
ma-souss-agadir-taghazout--le-the-a-la-m.text: Morocco’s most popular drink, atay: making a good mint tea is considered an art.

ma-souss-agadir-taghazout--agadir-recons.title: Agadir, rebuilt
ma-souss-agadir-taghazout--agadir-recons.text: Destroyed by an earthquake in 1960, the city was rebuilt to anti-seismic standards; it is Morocco’s biggest seaside resort.

ma-essaouira-sidikaouki--le-festival-gna.title: Gnaoua Festival
ma-essaouira-sidikaouki--le-festival-gna.text: Founded in 1998, this yearly festival brings Gnaoua musicians from Morocco and guest artists from around the world to Essaouira.

ma-essaouira-sidikaouki--le-bois-de-thuy.title: Thuya wood
ma-essaouira-sidikaouki--le-bois-de-thuy.text: Thuya marquetry is the craft that supports most of Essaouira: in 2011, 58% of the town’s craftsmen worked this wood.

ma-essaouira-sidikaouki--les-vents-de-la.title: Winds of the bay
ma-essaouira-sidikaouki--les-vents-de-la.text: Strong winds blow almost all the time in the bay: a renowned windsurfing and kitesurfing spot, with a World Cup stage.

ma-essaouira-sidikaouki--sidi-kaouki.title: Sidi Kaouki
ma-essaouira-sidikaouki--sidi-kaouki.text: 25 km south of Essaouira, this small town is a windsurfing spot thanks to strong, steady winds and a moderate swell.

cv-sal--la-cachupa.title: Cachupa
cv-sal--la-cachupa.text: Cape Verde’s national dish: a stew of maize, beans and fish or meat; leftovers are refried for breakfast with an egg.

cv-sal--sal-le-sel.title: Sal, “the salt”
cv-sal--sal-le-sel.text: Discovered on 3 December 1460, the island was called Chã (“flat”); it became Sal when two big salt pans were found there.

cv-sal--le-grogue-et-le-ponche.title: Grogue and ponche
cv-sal--le-grogue-et-le-ponche.text: Grogue is a sugar-cane spirit, popular in Cape Verde; it is the base of ponche, a kind of punch.

cv-sal--le-pastel.title: Pastel
cv-sal--le-pastel.text: A small fried turnover filled with fish or meat, served as a starter in Cape Verde.

sc-ladigue-praslin--la-charrette-a-b-ufs.title: Ox cart
sc-ladigue-praslin--la-charrette-a-b-ufs.text: On La Digue you hire bicycles near the jetty; the other way to get around is the ox cart, whose slow pace suits the island.

sc-ladigue-praslin--la-vallee-de-mai.title: Vallée de Mai
sc-ladigue-praslin--la-vallee-de-mai.text: A 19.5-hectare palm forest on Praslin, a UNESCO site since 1983; home to the coco de mer and five other endemic palms.

sc-ladigue-praslin--le-moutya.title: Moutya
sc-ladigue-praslin--le-moutya.text: An African dance close to the séga: dancers follow a goatskin drum heated over a fire before the start; the rhythm is slow, then speeds up.

sc-ladigue-praslin--la-cuisine-de-poisso.title: Fish cooking
sc-ladigue-praslin--la-cuisine-de-poisso.text: Fish has hundreds of recipes here: curry, raw with lemon, grilled or steamed; fried octopus and garlic lobster too.

us-hawaii-oahu--eddie-aikau.title: Eddie Aikau
us-hawaii-oahu--eddie-aikau.text: The Eddie Aikau Big Wave Invitational, “The Eddie”, is named after him; he died in 1978 during the voyage of the canoe Hōkūleʻa.

us-hawaii-oahu--duke-kahanamoku.title: Duke Kahanamoku
us-hawaii-oahu--duke-kahanamoku.text: Born under the Kingdom of Hawaii, this swimmer held the 100 m freestyle world record and won five Olympic medals (1912, 1920, 1924).

us-hawaii-oahu--lei-day.title: Lei Day
us-hawaii-oahu--lei-day.text: On 1 May, the lei festival, official since 1929; each island has its flower, yellow ilima for Oahu. Big ceremony at Kapiʻolani Park.

us-hawaii-oahu--le-plate-lunch.title: Plate lunch
us-hawaii-oahu--le-plate-lunch.text: A typical Hawaiian meal: one or two scoops of rice, macaroni salad and a dish often Japanese in style, like chicken katsu.

cr-nicoya--le-gallo-pinto.title: Gallo pinto
cr-nicoya--le-gallo-pinto.text: “Spotted rooster” in Spanish: rice and beans cooked with garlic, oregano and onion. National dish of Costa Rica and Nicaragua.

cr-nicoya--une-zone-bleue.title: A blue zone
cr-nicoya--une-zone-bleue.text: Nicoya is cited among the “blue zones” (exceptional longevity). The idea is unproven: those born after 1930 do not live longer there.

cr-nicoya--les-chorotega.title: The Chorotega
cr-nicoya--les-chorotega.text: Before the Spanish arrived, the Chorotega people lived here, in towns such as Zapatí, Nacaome and Nicopasaya.

cr-nicoya--le-refuge-d-ostional.title: Ostional refuge
cr-nicoya--le-refuge-d-ostional.text: An 85.7 km² refuge, protected since 1982, with nesting beaches for the olive ridley turtle: per the WWF, one of the two main sites in the world.

id-bali-bukit--le-temple-d-uluwatu.title: Uluwatu temple
id-bali-bukit--le-temple-d-uluwatu.text: Built on the edge (ulu) of a 70 m cliff (watu); legend says this rock is part of the petrified boat of the goddess Dewi Danu.

id-bali-bukit--le-kecak.title: Kecak
id-bali-bukit--le-kecak.text: A dance sung by a chorus of men, performed daily at 6 p.m. in Balinese temples such as Uluwatu and Tanah Lot.

id-bali-bukit--melasti.title: Melasti
id-bali-bukit--melasti.text: Before Nyepi, Balinese Hindus go to the sea to purify themselves: they symbolically cast the past’s evil into it and wash the temples’ sacred objects.

id-bali-bukit--nyepi-le-jour-du-silence.title: Nyepi, the day of silence
id-bali-bukit--nyepi-le-jour-du-silence.text: The Balinese new year: silence, fasting and meditation. No one, tourists included, goes on the beaches or the streets; the airport closes.

nz-raglan--waikeri.title: Waikeri
nz-raglan--waikeri.text: The traditional name of Manu Bay is Waikeri, “turning waters”; this surf spot appears in the film The Endless Summer (1966).

nz-raglan--le-film-the-endless-summer.title: The film The Endless Summer
nz-raglan--le-film-the-endless-summer.text: Bruce Brown’s 1966 documentary: the Californian surfers Mike Hynson and Robert August travel the world, Manu Bay included.

nz-raglan--le-hangi.title: Hāngī
nz-raglan--le-hangi.text: Māori cooking in an earth oven (umu): stones are heated, then the food is buried; still used for big occasions.

nz-raglan--le-mont-karioi.title: Mount Karioi
nz-raglan--le-mont-karioi.text: An extinct volcano 2.4 million years old, 8 km south-west of Raglan, the first of six aligned volcanoes, the biggest being Pirongia.

jp-kanagawa-shonan--le-grand-bouddha-de-.title: Great Buddha of Kamakura
jp-kanagawa-shonan--le-grand-bouddha-de-.text: A bronze statue 13.35 m high and about 93 tonnes, dated to around 1252 in the temple records; it is hollow and can be visited inside.

jp-kanagawa-shonan--le-yabusame.title: Yabusame
jp-kanagawa-shonan--le-yabusame.text: Mounted archery: the archer shoots three arrows at three wooden targets. Seen at Tsurugaoka Hachiman-gū shrine, in Kamakura.

jp-kanagawa-shonan--l-ile-d-enoshima.title: Enoshima island
jp-kanagawa-shonan--l-ile-d-enoshima.text: Linked by a 389 m bridge, the island is dedicated to Benzaiten, goddess of music, said to have raised it from the sea in the 6th century.

jp-kanagawa-shonan--kamakura-capitale-de.title: Kamakura, capital of the shoguns
jp-kanagawa-shonan--kamakura-capitale-de.text: In 1192, shogun Minamoto no Yoritomo made Kamakura, then a mere town, his capital; his government ruled the country until 1333.

br-santacatarina-floripa--l-heritage-aco.title: Azorean heritage
br-santacatarina-floripa--l-heritage-aco.text: In the mid-18th century, thousands of Azoreans migrated here; Florianópolis still shows it: houses, crafts, cooking.

br-santacatarina-floripa--les-huitres-de.title: Oysters of Ribeirão da Ilha
br-santacatarina-floripa--les-huitres-de.text: This district of Florianópolis, one of the oldest Azorean settlements, is Brazil’s biggest oyster producer.

br-santacatarina-floripa--joaquina-et-se.title: Joaquina and its dunes
br-santacatarina-floripa--joaquina-et-se.text: The beach, prized by surfers for the quality of its waves, is surrounded by the Lagoa da Conceição dunes municipal nature park.

br-santacatarina-floripa--praia-mole.title: Praia Mole
br-santacatarina-floripa--praia-mole.text: A 960-metre beach on the island’s east coast, known for drawing young people, surfers and paragliders.

zones.us-hawaii-kona: Kona y la bahía de Kealakekua
zones.fr-verdon-saintecroix: Lago de Sainte-Croix y el país de Moustiers
zones.fr-paysbasque-cotebasque: Biarritz, Anglet y San Juan de Luz
zones.fr-provence-calanques: Calanques de Marsella y de Cassis
zones.gp-basseterre-cousteau: Reserva Cousteau y costa a sotavento
zones.ie-clare-lahinch: Lahinch y el condado de Clare
zones.gr-crete-balos: Balos y la bahía de Kissamos
zones.hr-dalmatie-brac: Bol y la isla de Brač
zones.br-santacatarina-floripa: Joaquina, Praia Mole y la isla de Santa Catarina

fr-landes-hossegor--le-pastis-landais.title: El pastis landais
fr-landes-hossegor--le-pastis-landais.text: Brioche con flor de azahar, ron o vainilla, reservada durante mucho tiempo a las bodas y a las fiestas del pueblo.

fr-landes-hossegor--la-course-landaise.title: La course landaise
fr-landes-hossegor--la-course-landaise.text: Los écarteurs esquivan a la vaca en el último momento, sin darle muerte. Anima las fiestas locales de marzo a octubre.

fr-landes-hossegor--baine.title: Baïne
fr-landes-hossegor--baine.text: Palabra gascona para la cubeta de agua paralela a la playa, donde la corriente puede volverse peligrosa según la marea.

fr-paysbasque-guethary--l-axoa.title: El axoa
fr-paysbasque-guethary--l-axoa.text: Ternera en dados, estofada con pimiento, cebolla y chile de Espelette: un plato de feria y de fiesta en el País Vasco.

fr-paysbasque-guethary--kaixo.title: Kaixo
fr-paysbasque-guethary--kaixo.text: «Buenos días» u «hola» en euskera, para decir con una sonrisa.

fr-paysbasque-guethary--les-fetes-de-la-.title: Las fiestas de San Nicolás
fr-paysbasque-guethary--les-fetes-de-la-.text: Las fiestas patronales de Guéthary se celebran cada año en diciembre, en torno a san Nicolás.

fr-paysbasque-guethary--la-pelote-au-gra.title: La pelota con gran chistera
fr-paysbasque-guethary--la-pelote-au-gra.text: El club L’Olharroa, nacido en 1922, es apodado la Meca del gran chistera: se juega en el frontón del pueblo.

fr-finistere-penhors--le-pardon-de-penho.title: El pardon de Penhors
fr-finistere-penhors--le-pardon-de-penho.text: El pardon de Penhors, en Pouldreuzic, se celebra el primer domingo de septiembre: procesión, misa y bendición, como todo pardon bretón.

fr-finistere-penhors--le-fest-noz.title: El fest-noz
fr-finistere-penhors--le-fest-noz.text: Noche de baile bretona, abierta a todos: te unes a la gavotte o al an dro después de mirar los pasos.

fr-finistere-penhors--le-far-breton.title: El far bretón
fr-finistere-penhors--le-far-breton.text: Pastel de huevos, leche y mantequilla semisalada, a menudo con las ciruelas pasas que los marineros bretones traían de Burdeos.

fr-finistere-penhors--la-coiffe-bigouden.title: La coiffe bigoudène
fr-finistere-penhors--la-coiffe-bigouden.text: Alta unos treinta centímetros, ya solo se lleva en los pardons, fiestas y festivales.

fr-var-portcros--l-aioli.title: El aïoli
fr-var-portcros--l-aioli.text: Bacalao y verduras servidos con una salsa de ajo machacado y aceite de oliva: un plato emblemático de la Provenza.

fr-var-portcros--une-peche-encadree.title: Una pesca regulada
fr-var-portcros--une-peche-encadree.text: En la isla, la pesca sigue siendo tradicional pero regulada: carta desde 1999 para 24 profesionales, autorización anual para aficionados.

fr-var-portcros--la-vigie.title: La Vigie
fr-var-portcros--la-vigie.text: Antiguo semáforo al que se llega por la antigua ruta estratégica, con vistas al archipiélago y al macizo de los Maures.

fr-corse-rondinara--le-fiadone.title: El fiadone
fr-corse-rondinara--le-fiadone.text: Pastel fresco de brocciu, azúcar, huevos y limón, un postre emblemático de Córcega.

fr-corse-rondinara--les-polyphonies-cors.title: Las polifonías corsas
fr-corse-rondinara--les-polyphonies-cors.text: Canto a tres voces a cappella, nacido de la vida de los pueblos y los pastores: veladas, peregrinaciones y fiestas lo mantienen vivo.

fr-corse-rondinara--la-semaine-sainte-a-.title: La Semana Santa en Bonifacio
fr-corse-rondinara--la-semaine-sainte-a-.text: Las cofradías organizan procesiones muy concurridas durante la Semana Santa, y los oficios de Tinieblas.

pt-ericeira--l-oursin-d-ericeira.title: El erizo de Ericeira
pt-ericeira--l-oursin-d-ericeira.text: Especialidad de la ciudad: los restaurantes del pueblo cocinan el erizo de varias maneras durante el festival que le está dedicado.

pt-ericeira--le-festival-international-d.title: El festival internacional del erizo
pt-ericeira--le-festival-international-d.text: Degustaciones, showcooking y talleres en el mercado municipal de Ericeira: la edición de 2026 fue del 24 de abril al 3 de mayo.

pt-ericeira--reserve-mondiale-de-surf.title: Reserva mundial de surf
pt-ericeira--reserve-mondiale-de-surf.text: Desde octubre de 2011, la costa de Ericeira lleva el título de reserva mundial de surf, concedido por Save the Waves.

es-minorque-macarella--sant-joan-a-ciuta.title: Sant Joan en Ciutadella
es-minorque-macarella--sant-joan-a-ciuta.text: El 23 y 24 de junio, jinetes y caballos menorquines desfilan en Ciutadella, con «bots» en los que el caballo se encabrita.

es-minorque-macarella--le-fromage-de-mao.title: El queso de Maó
es-minorque-macarella--le-fromage-de-mao.text: Queso de vaca con corteza anaranjada frotada con aceite de oliva y pimentón, protegido por una DOP desde 1985.

es-minorque-macarella--la-caldereta-de-l.title: La caldereta de langosta
es-minorque-macarella--la-caldereta-de-l.text: Sopa de langosta a fuego lento, un plato típico de Menorca.

es-minorque-macarella--pomada.title: Pomada
es-minorque-macarella--pomada.text: Ginebra de Menorca mezclada con limonada, que se bebe durante las fiestas patronales.

es-minorque-macarella--le-cami-de-cavall.title: El Camí de Cavalls
es-minorque-macarella--le-cami-de-cavall.text: Sendero que rodea la isla a pie (GR 223), antiguo camino que unía las torres de defensa.

gr-zakynthos-navagio--la-fete-de-saint-d.title: La fiesta de san Dionisio
gr-zakynthos-navagio--la-fete-de-saint-d.text: El 24 de agosto, por la tarde, las reliquias de san Dionisio, patrón de la isla, recorren en procesión la ciudad de Zante.

gr-zakynthos-navagio--le-raisin-de-corin.title: La pasa de Corinto de Zante
gr-zakynthos-navagio--le-raisin-de-corin.text: Uva pequeña, dulce y sin pepitas, nacida en la isla: con el aceite de oliva, es uno de sus grandes productos.

gr-zakynthos-navagio--les-produits-du-te.title: Los productos de la tierra
gr-zakynthos-navagio--les-produits-du-te.text: Aceite de oliva, miel de tomillo, pasas de Corinto y vino se venden en puestos al borde de las carreteras y en los pueblos.

gr-zakynthos-navagio--le-poete-solomos.title: El poeta Solomos
gr-zakynthos-navagio--le-poete-solomos.text: Una estatua del poeta Dionýsios Solomós adorna la plaza principal de Zante, y un museo lleva su nombre en la plaza de San Marcos.

gb-gower-rhossili--le-laverbread.title: El laverbread
gb-gower-rhossili--le-laverbread.text: Puré espeso de alga porphyra hervida durante horas, llamado «bara lawr» en galés.

gb-gower-rhossili--les-coques-de-penclaw.title: Los berberechos de Penclawdd
gb-gower-rhossili--les-coques-de-penclaw.text: Familias de Penclawdd recogen los berberechos del Burry Inlet desde hace generaciones; se venden en el mercado de Swansea.

gb-gower-rhossili--l-agneau-de-pre-sale-.title: El cordero de pasto salado de Gower
gb-gower-rhossili--l-agneau-de-pre-sale-.text: Pace samphire y lavanda de mar; DOP en el Reino Unido en 2021 y en la Unión Europea en 2023.

gb-gower-rhossili--worm-s-head.title: Worm’s Head
gb-gower-rhossili--worm-s-head.text: Dos islotes, Inner Head y Outer Head, a los que solo se llega con marea baja.

gb-gower-rhossili--gallois-au-nord-angla.title: Galés al norte, inglés al sur
gb-gower-rhossili--gallois-au-nord-angla.text: El norte de Gower cuenta con muchos galófonos, mientras que el sur es tradicionalmente anglófono.

pf-societe-tahiti--le-heiva-i-tahiti.title: El Heiva i Tahiti
pf-societe-tahiti--le-heiva-i-tahiti.text: Cada julio, unos quince días de concursos de canto y danza, y de deportes ancestrales como el va’a, en la plaza To’atā.

pf-societe-tahiti--le-poisson-cru.title: El pescado crudo
pf-societe-tahiti--le-poisson-cru.text: Pescado marinado en lima y leche de coco: el plato de la isla que hay que probar primero.

pf-societe-tahiti--le-tamaaraa.title: El tamaaraa
pf-societe-tahiti--le-tamaaraa.text: Festín de cerdo, pescado y fruto del árbol del pan cocidos al vapor en un horno de tierra, para las grandes ocasiones familiares.

pf-societe-tahiti--la-fleur-de-tiare.title: La flor de tiaré
pf-societe-tahiti--la-fleur-de-tiare.text: Una flor en la oreja izquierda dice que no buscas compañía; en la derecha, que estás disponible.

cl-pichilemu--la-fete-du-cochayuyo.title: La fiesta del cochayuyo
cl-pichilemu--la-fete-du-cochayuyo.text: Cinco días de platos a base de cochayuyo, un alga marina; el último día fue el domingo 26 de julio en 2026.

cl-pichilemu--les-fiestas-patrias.title: Las Fiestas Patrias
cl-pichilemu--les-fiestas-patrias.text: Hacia el 18 de septiembre, Pichilemu celebra la fiesta nacional: juegos tradicionales, cocina, música y baile, de día y de noche.

cl-pichilemu--empanadas-et-completos.title: Empanadas y completos
cl-pichilemu--empanadas-et-completos.text: Las empanadas y los «completos» son los dos grandes clásicos para llevar en Pichilemu.

cl-pichilemu--le-parc-agustin-ross.title: El parque Agustín Ross
cl-pichilemu--le-parc-agustin-ross.text: El parque y centro cultural Agustín Ross es uno de los cinco monumentos nacionales de Pichilemu.

br-noronha--le-centre-historique.title: El centro histórico
br-noronha--le-centre-historique.text: La Vila dos Remédios y la capilla São Pedro dos Pescadores son patrimonio cultural de Brasil, declarado por el Iphan en 2017.

br-noronha--l-acai.title: El açaí
br-noronha--l-acai.text: Después del buceo, nada como un bol de açaí servido en el puerto, con granola y plátanos.

mx-islamujeres--le-tik-n-chik.title: El tik-n-chik
mx-islamujeres--le-tik-n-chik.text: Pescado entero marinado en achiote y luego a la parrilla: es el plato estrella de la isla.

mx-islamujeres--punta-sur.title: Punta Sur
mx-islamujeres--punta-sur.text: En el extremo sur, las ruinas de un antiguo faro y de un templo de Ixchel, diosa de la fertilidad.

mx-islamujeres--isla-mujeres.title: Isla Mujeres
mx-islamujeres--isla-mujeres.text: El nombre de la isla significa «isla de las Mujeres» en español.

sn-dakar-ouakam--le-ceebu-jen.title: El ceebu jën
sn-dakar-ouakam--le-ceebu-jen.text: Arroz con pescado y verduras de temporada, nacido entre los pescadores de Saint-Louis, inscrito en la UNESCO en 2021; suele comerse con las manos.

sn-dakar-ouakam--teranga.title: Teranga
sn-dakar-ouakam--teranga.text: Palabra wolof a menudo traducida como «hospitalidad»: compartir la comida y acoger al extranjero en casa.

sn-dakar-ouakam--un-village-lebou.title: Un pueblo lebou
sn-dakar-ouakam--un-village-lebou.text: Ouakam es uno de los cuatro pueblos lebou originales de la península de Cabo Verde, junto con Yoff, Ngor y Hann.

sn-dakar-ouakam--la-mosquee-de-la-divini.title: La mezquita de la Divinidad
sn-dakar-ouakam--la-mosquee-de-la-divini.text: Un hombre santo dice haber recibido en sueños, el 28 de junio de 1973, la orden de construir esta mezquita a orillas del océano.

au-whitsundays-whitehaven--le-great-barr.title: El Great Barrier Reef Festival
au-whitsundays-whitehaven--le-great-barr.text: Cuatro días en Airlie Beach con fuegos artificiales, regata de barcos reciclados y desfile callejero: del 31 de julio al 2 de agosto en 2026.

au-whitsundays-whitehaven--la-hamilton-i.title: La Hamilton Island Race Week
au-whitsundays-whitehaven--la-hamilton-i.text: Gran regata en alta mar, descrita como la más importante de Australia: del 15 al 22 de agosto en 2026, con animación en la marina.

au-whitsundays-whitehaven--le-marche-d-a.title: El mercado de Airlie Beach
au-whitsundays-whitehaven--le-marche-d-a.text: Cada sábado de 7 h a 13 h, frente al mar: recuerdos, café, fruta fresca y arte local.

au-whitsundays-whitehaven--le-ngaro-trac.title: El Ngaro Track
au-whitsundays-whitehaven--le-ngaro-trac.text: Abierto en 2026, este sendero de 32 km va de Whitehaven a Hill Inlet; los propietarios tradicionales piden caminar por él con respeto.
